editorial.summary: The third consecutive Big Bear episode is an unusually useful lesson in transcript epistemology. Its ordinary first half covers a struggling recreational hockey team, the first Ranch night, Bill Poon's snoring, Steve Lee's masturbation-abstinence promise, Sizzler, a bathroom knock first blamed on a ghost and then traced to Val, a sleep-deprived failed fishing hike, Bobby Lee's gaming and phone fixation, the recurring 'funnier Lee brother' provocation, communal cooking, and the allocation of Ranch bedrooms. After David Choe and Asa Akira truthfully say they talked until sunrise and eventually shared a very large bed with a boundary between them, they spend nearly an hour claiming the encounter became sex. The performance accumulates dry-humping, ejaculation, pregnancy risk, Tony roleplay, guilt, home-wrecking, Cialis, secrecy and responsibility details. Other participants react in real time, some condemning David, some assigning responsibility to Asa, some sexualizing the story, and some remaining skeptical. None of those reactions corroborates the alleged affair. A timestamped text exchange read aloud near the end shows David and Asa planned immediately before recording to tell everyone they had sex and reveal 'JK' at the end. Within Episode 136 they then deny sex and reconstruct the night as conversation, couch/bed logistics, Robocop 2 and sleep. Episode 139 later claims that denial was itself the middle layer of a planned double prank and re-alleges that sex occurred. The archive therefore records a three-state sequence—alleged, denied, re-alleged—rather than declaring either the confession or denial independently verified. Every embedded sexual detail remains attributed to the speakers and later supersession state, never promoted to external fact. This validates a three-layer product design: immutable transcript, claim-level correction/provenance, and interpretation that can change when later evidence arrives. Other meaningful threads include correction of Bobby's claimed honesty with his mother, porn/obscenity-law discussion, private spouse boundaries, the cast's invented racial-code callback, body/food pressure, fertility misinformation explicitly mocked as feelings-based science, and the closing description of the podcast as a diary of changing beliefs. All seventeen cleaner edits are empty records. Automated Sizzler-to-Twizzler substitutions are rejected. Named turns remain unpublished because held-out second-speaker detection failed.
